findings.title: Generated key is 49 chars but column allows only 48
findings.detail: secrets.token_hex(20) returns 40 hex characters. 'mcp_live_' is 9 characters. Total: 49 characters. The column is defined as String(48) / VARCHAR(48). Every call to _new_mcp_key() — on first enable and on regenerate — will produce a value that exceeds the column limit, causing PostgreSQL to raise DataError (value too long for type character varying(48)) and returning a 500 on those endpoints.
findings.correction: Either (a) change String(48) to String(49) in company.py and VARCHAR(48) to VARCHAR(49) in the SQL migration, keeping token_hex(20); or (b) change token_hex(20) to token_hex(19) (yielding 47-char keys) while leaving the 48-char column. The mock DEMO_KEY of 48 chars confirms 48 was the intended column size, so option (b) is the more consistent fix.
